classification.difficultyReason: One step: the given 62° is measured from the vertical, so the student must take the depression angle from the horizontal as 90° − 62°. No triangle sum is needed. It matches p5-q5 part a.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle of depression, measured down from the horizontal to the line of sight.
$$\begin{align*}\theta+62^{\circ}&=90^{\circ}\\\theta&=90^{\circ}-62^{\circ}\\&=28^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles in a right angle.
